title: Spectral Signatures of Large Language Models

problem.claim: Systematically managing and quantifying publicly available large language models at scale is difficult, including for model lineage tracing, licensing, and evaluation.

gap.claim: Task-specific benchmarks are insufficient because large language models differ widely in architectures, scales, and training procedures.

contributions.claim: The paper adopts spectral shape-based metrics grounded in Heavy-Tailed Self-Regularization theory to manage and quantify large language models.
It represents each model with a compact spectral signature based on the shape of its weight empirical spectral density.
It curates a large and diverse corpus of major open-source large language model families for systematic metric benchmarking across models and downstream tasks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the spectral signature captures intrinsic properties of pretrained models and remains robust during post-training.
The authors report that the metric is data-free, computationally efficient, and scale-invariant.
The authors report that the spectral signature supports model-lineage tracking, unsupervised clustering of similar models, and performance quantification.

narrative_sequence.summary: Large-scale management and quantification of publicly available large language models creates challenges.
Task-specific benchmarks do not adequately address model diversity in architecture, scale, and training procedure.
The paper uses spectral shape-based metrics and weight spectral-density shape information to construct model signatures.
A diverse open-source model corpus is used to benchmark spectral and non-spectral metrics across models and downstream tasks.
The signature is reported to support lineage tracking, clustering, performance quantification, and broad performance-trend analysis.

source_observation.claim: A model-level signature based on weight spectral-density shape is described as robust during post-training and independent of data.

interpretation.claim: Structural model properties may provide a compact basis for comparing models across changing training states.

application.claim: Use model-internal spectral summaries as retrieval or organization features for large model collections when task-specific evaluation is insufficient.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how well the signature transfers across architectures, scales, training procedures, or tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluated model families, model counts, tasks, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not provide details of the spectral metrics, experimental protocol, or limitations.
